awB0_intro:

awB2_slider_glide_trigger:
Psycho Slider glide trigger in the Angkor Wat outer east area.

The actor waits until event flag $016B is set (WaitOnFlagWord, sense 1), stores $000A in $0E (the glide length, in units of 16 px: LockPlayerForGlide) and JumpFar's to slider_glide.SliderGlideTriggerNorthMain. From there it runs as a north Psycho Slider glide trigger (see the slider_glide block note).
awB3_ledge_jump_trigger:
Angkor Wat outer north (scene $B3): one-shot trigger that changes the map and then makes the player jump (LedgeJumpEntry).

Spawned once, by scene_B3_actors. The actor dies at once when flag word $016E is set. Otherwise it waits (SetEntryHere) until the player stands in the tile box (6A, 0C)-(6F, 0D), then: ORs $CFFC into joypadMaskStd 20 times (LoopStart #14), plays the sound pair #$0F0F, applies BG change #6E (StageBgChange / ApplyBgChange), sets flag word $016E, writes player_character.LedgeJumpEntry into the player actor (address at +$00, bank byte at +$02, $08 and $2A zeroed), sets playerFlags $0800 and dies.

The jump starts because this script writes LedgeJumpEntry, not because of a type $08 cell. BG change #6E was not decoded. Mesen2 (scene $B3, player poked into the tile box): within 10 frames the player's entry word became LedgeJumpEntry (animation $18, playerFlags $0800) and the fall ended at x 1400, y 112 after starting from x 1736, y 204 (not traced further); a before / after diff of the collision map and the layer-0 tilemap showed no changed cell, so what the BG change draws is unknown.
awB4_snake_pit_entry: Snake pit entry of Angkor Wat (scene $B4). Each time the player stands at pixel (0578,0010) the actor writes player_character.loc_02C63B into the player's entry word (the fall), sets bit $0200 and clears bit $0008 of the player's flags $10, zeroes the player's $08 and $2A and sets playerFlags $0800. The first time ($B5 clear) it also sets $B5, writes TM = $15, CGADSUB = $A1 and COLDATA = $FF, waits 180 ticks (WaitByte #B3) and spawns oneshot_backdrop_fade_out_1C. Afterwards it polls the buttons of mask $0F01: inside tiles (3D,0C)-(43,1B) or (43,06)-(5D,1B) it plays sound ch2 $08 every 8 frames.

awBC_blinding_light: Crystal shrine light of Angkor Wat (scene $BC). The first time ($B7 clear) the actor sets $B7, locks the player ($CFFC), waits 30 ticks (WaitByte #1D), prints 'Setting one foot inside, the floating crystal started to glow!' and unlocks. Whether or not the narration ran, it then tests the Black Crystal Glasses (item $1C): with the glasses equipped at that moment no flash runs. Otherwise it waits 20 ticks (WaitByte #13), spawns oneshot_palette_flash_18, waits 180 ticks (WaitByte #B3) and polls the equip test every frame; when the glasses are equipped it spawns oneshot_palette_flash_19 once and parks in a polling loop that spawns flash 18 again only if the glasses are unequipped later.
awBC_bouncing_crystal:

awBD_fall_trigger: Fall trigger of Angkor Wat (scenes $BB and $BD). awBF_spirit_guide: Spirit guide on the pinnacle of Angkor Wat (scene $BF, tile (0F,0B)). $BE set: dies. Otherwise a solid prop with the interact handler. $BD clear: the handler prints 'Will.. I've been waiting for you to come for thousands of years...' (the vision dialog), sets $BD and queues scene $C0 (future_vision_cutscene, which returns to scene $BF at (00F8,00C0)). $BD set (after the return): locks the player ($FFFC), prints 'Huh? What was that? That is the new world...', writes CGADSUB = $15, spawns oneshot_palette_flash_18, clears the solid tiles (0F,0A) and (10,0A), spawns oneshot_palette_flash_19, prints 'When the blinding light stopped, I stood quietly, as if nothing had happened. Then I found the Gorgon flower held tightly within my hand...' and gives item $1D. On a full inventory it removes a Red Jewel (jewelsCollected +1 in BCD) or a herb first ('Let me take care of one of your Red Jewels...'); with neither item the branch code_089B27 falls into the Red Jewel exchange without a check. After the gift it shows 'You have the Gorgon Flower!', sets $BE, unlocks and dies.
camera_delta_oscillator:
Per-frame actor: cameraDeltaX = cameraTargetX, and bit 9 ($0200) of the frame counter $0036 (incremented once per frame in the NMI) selects INC (bit set) or DEC (bit clear) of cameraDeltaY.

Bit 9 flips every 512 frames, so cameraDeltaY ramps up 512 steps and back down 512 steps (about 8.5 s per half at 60 Hz): a slow vertical drift.
cameraDeltaX / Y are not the camera itself: camera_tilemap copies them into effectScrollH / V in layer-1 delta mode ($06EF bit 2), and camera_scroll actors compute them as parallax ratios of cameraTargetX / Y.
No extracted script references this actor by label and the ROM holds no 16-bit or 24-bit pointer to its header or entry (no scene actor record, spawn operand, table word or instruction operand), so nothing spawns it.

dark_space:
Dark Space portal (Bank 08, 579230-579495): the glowing portal object that leads to the Gaia hub (scene $E6, system/dark_space/sE6_gaia). The actor is only a trigger and an effect: the scene change itself is done by the warp rectangle of the room (a scene-warp row to scene $E6) once the actor has moved the player onto it.

=== PLACEMENT ===

dark_space2 is spawned by 31 scene spawn rows, dark_space by one (Dao, scene_C3_actors). pyCC_dark_space_portal, ec12_aqueduct_dark_space, gw88_tomb_dark_space and dm40_hidden_dark_space spawn DarkSpacePortalInit directly with $24 already set (1, or 3 in the pyramid when $0E is not $72). The scene spawn byte is odd in all 32 rows (12 x #01, 14 x #03, 6 x #05), so the engine leaves param >> 1 in $0E: variant 0, 1 or 2. The two init stubs move that into $24 and then replace $0E with the OAM attribute word: $3000 (sprite priority 3, Dao only) or $2000 (priority 2). The variant is the Gaia room layout: sE6_gaia accepts 0 to 3 (0 basic, 1 transformation statues, 2 ability, 3 special = layout 1 with the form-dependent logic).

=== PORTAL ANIMATION ===

DarkSpacePortalInit sets up the sprite (spriteset_pickups_effects frame #24 closed), makes the tile solid (MarkSolidHere), sets Flags12 $0004 (pause-filter immunity), Flags10 $0B00, extendedFlags $0200 (radar dot) and spawns the monitor child. The portal then loops: closed while the player is not near; when the player is within 5 tiles (|dx| and |dy| both < 81 pixels) it plays the opening animation #1F once and holds the open frame #20 while the player stays near; when he leaves, the closing animation #21 plays and it returns to the closed frame.

=== ENTRY (monitor child) ===

DarkSpaceInteractionMonitor (hidden child, flags $2300, $24 = variant) runs every frame, but not while displayModeFlags bit $0080 (display-filter actor mode) is set. It tests BranchIfPlayerInRelTiles ( -1, 0, 1, 1 ): the player's tile offset from the portal must satisfy -1 < dx <= 1 and 0 < dy <= 1. Then BranchIfPressed $0801 (raw Up) leads to DarkSpaceMonitorStartWarp, which runs in the MONITOR's context (Y = $04 is the portal):
1. joypadMaskStd |= $CFFC (every button except Select and Start; the ROM has $CFF0 and db-us/transforms.json widens it, as in the other scripts) and the PLAYER's $10 |= $2000: the player becomes hidden (SortActorsByDepth skips actors with bit $2000).
2. The monitor's own X/Y := the player's X/Y, SFX $0C on both channels, the monitor's own $2000 cleared (it becomes visible) and animation #1C of spriteset_pickups_effects plays once at the player's spot, then 29 more frames.
3. The player's X/Y := the portal's X/Y; playerXPos = X - 8, playerYPos = Y - 16 and the tile words playerXTile/YTile (>> 4). That puts the player one tile north of the portal, which is where the room's E6 warp rectangle lies, so the normal warp check fires.
4. gfxCacheIdxB := $0101 (exit and enter speed 1), gfxCacheIdxA := $0200 (exit effect 0 = fade, enter effect 2 = mosaic), layerPriorityFlag |= $0200 (camera frozen / chests off while the warp runs) and globalScriptIndex := the variant for sE6_gaia's layout switch. The monitor then idles (SetEntryHere + RTL).
idle_sprite_display:
Static 5-gem pickup actor: shows spriteset_pickups_effects frame #06 and carries item ID $85 in chatPtr. No scene actor list or COP spawn in extracted/ refers to it by name.

Header bytes: animation state 0 and flags word $0020 (ORed with $4000 by InitActorFromSceneData, so $4020). Bit $0020 marks the actor friendly: when the player overlaps it ApplyInteractionDamage routes to InteractionDamage_NPCChat, which calls GiveItemToPlayer(chatPtr). Item $85 is '+5 gems' (cap 999, SFX #22); DropBodyGem5 spawns the same $85 with the same frame #06, so this is the stationary version of that gem.

Pass structure: init stores chatPtr and the metasprite, SetEntryHere marks the re-entry address, then StageSpriteFrame #06 and AnimOnce run on every pass. No SetSpritePalette is issued here, unlike the gem spawners, which use palette #00.
jeweler_gem:
Jeweler Gem: the Red Jewel collector NPC (Bank 08, 577187-577682). Placed with spawn parameter #01 in scenes $01 (South Cape), $32 (Freejia), $6B, $7B, $9B and $C3, one record each; every placement runs this same code.

=== SPAWN (JewelerGemEntry) ===

Event flag $E8 is the Solid Arm flag: sEA_solid_arm sets it before its intro dialog (after the scene's lock and the WaitWord #$0120 wait, with no fight needed), so from the first entry into scene $EA on, Gem no longer appears (JewelerDie) in the six scenes that spawn him ($01, $32, $6B, $7B, $9B, $C3). Otherwise the spawn parameter in $0E picks an 8-frame animation group (all six records pass #01, which gives group 0): the animation index $28 is set to group x 8 + 2 (it is an animation index, not a sprite frame). $0E is then replaced by $3000, the OAM attribute word. Gem marks his tile solid, registers JewelerInteract as his chatPtr and idles on a bare RTL; the shared talk handler in global_ambient_dispatcher runs JewelerInteract when the player presses the interact button (A in this build) facing him.

=== REWARD TIERS (JewelerInteract, JewelerCheck*) ===

JewelerInteract greets, prints the stored jewel count if it is non-zero and then walks the tiers in ascending order. A tier pays out when its 'given' flag is clear and jewelsCollected ($0AB0, a BCD value) has reached the threshold; each reward sets its flag and jumps to the next tier's check, so one talk can pay several tiers:
  3 jewels (flag $E9): Herb, item #06. If GiveItem fails the inventory-full text is printed and the talk ends without setting the flag.
  5 (flag $EA): playerDef + 1.
  8 (flag $EB): playerMaxHp + 1 and hpToHeal = 1, so UpdateHUD adds one current HP and the new point is filled. It is not an HP-bar flash.
  12 (flag $EC): playerStr + 1.
  20 (flag $ED): $0B16 = 1, the Psycho Dash upgrade level (attack_ability_system reads it: damage 5 at level 0, 10 at level 1).
  30 (flag $EE): $0B1C = 2, the Dark Friar upgrade level (damage 5 / 8 / 12; level 2 is the fully upgraded form).
  50 (no flag): warp to scene $E9, the sE9_mansion_intro scene that leads to the optional Solid Arm fight. There is no 'given' flag, so every talk with 50 or more jewels warps again; the jewels are not consumed and the menu below is never reached.
The dialogue string for the 8-jewel tier says 'Your Life Power will be raised' and then 'Your Strength is raised by one'; the code raises max HP (maxHp $0ACA 8 to 9 while the first page is on screen, hpToHeal $0B22 0 to 1 and HP 8 to 9 about 39 frames later) and leaves the strength and defence words ($0ADE, $0ADC) unchanged, so the second sentence is a text inconsistency (both pages observed on screen).

=== MENU AND JEWEL COUNTING ===

After the cascade (and any payouts) Gem shows the three-option menu: Just wanted to see you / Give you Red Jewels / See your inventory. The DialogueOptions result table is indexed 0 = B cancel, 1..3 = the options in order, so cancel and option 1 share JewelerCancelReply. 'Give you Red Jewels' (JewelerGiveJewelsOption) needs at least one item #01 in the inventory; JewelerCountJewels then counts the item #01 entries of the 16 inventory slots ($0AB4) with a BCD counter held in the absolute word $0000 (WRAM $7E:0000, scratch; not the actor's own DP $00), adds it to jewelsCollected in decimal mode, removes every jewel with RemoveItem in a loop and re-runs the tier check. 'See your inventory' prints the reward list and highlights (palette 4) each tier whose flag is set.

JewelerGoodbye_unused ('Well, see ya. Somewhere.') and its dialogue string have no reference anywhere: dead code.

nvAC_bones:
Bleached bones in the Native Village — recent death.

nvAC_bonfire:

nvAC_hamlet:
Hamlet the pig in the Native Village (scene $AC) and the effect actors of the Hamlet scene. Why such a sad look?'), plays sound $2121 with sprite loops of frames $AB and $AC and sets scratch $03 (Kara's cry; seven of the native NPCs start moving), waits for it to clear, starts music #11, prints 'Poor Hamlet... nvAC_hand_man:
Hand-offering man — non-verbal trust building.

Interactive NPC (~94 lines). "The man timidly held out his
hand... Take his hand? Yes/No" — cross-cultural trust
moment. "We don't understand each other's language, but
I think we agree..." Communication beyond words.
nvAC_kara:
Kara of the Native Village (scene $AC): the cutscene driver of the village. One script, five states chosen by persistent flags in this order: $B6 or $CF set: dies. $B2 set: stands at tile (12,0C) with 'I learned a word from the children. It seems that (Ramapoe) means (Hello) in this region.'. $AF set: the Hamlet scene. $B0 set: the sleep scene. $AD set: dies. $AC set: stands at tile (0B,0E) with the handler 'Strange. Not a soul here, and skeletons scattered around... Should we go into the houses?' (it sets $AD) and walks away when $AD is set. All clear: the arrival.

pyD0_ledge_jump_trigger:
Pyramid scenes $D0 (Meltdown A) and $D1 (Meltdown B), one placement each: a one-shot trigger that starts a ledge jump (LedgeJumpEntry). The actor has no HP counter, no hit test and no spawn, and only these two scenes place it.

The actor's $0E word (copied to $26) picks the variant: 0 uses flag word $0170 and BG change #70, anything else flag word $0171 and BG change #71. The actor dies at once when its flag word is set.

Gate (every pass): the player's body spriteset bank byte ($7F0008 + player slot) must be $95 (Will) or $8E (Freedan) and the player's animation index ($28) must be $1C, which LedgeJumpLand stages on a ledge-jump landing (the pose $1C is also staged by other player code); then BranchIfPlayerNear #01 decides whether the gate opens.

First pass ($24 = 0): sets $24 = 1, converts the actor's $14 / $16 to tile coordinates (the pixel values are saved in orbitAngle / orbitDiameter and restored), and draws metatiles #E8 and #E9 side by side with DrawMetatileHere at (tile X, tile Y - 1) and (tile X + 1, tile Y - 1). Measured in Mesen2 in scene $D0: the two cells (38, 20) and (39, 20), just north of the actor at tile (38, 21), change from collision type $00 to $0E (solid).

Second pass ($24 is 1, entered after the player has left the near zone and lands again): plays sound #15, applies BG change #70 / #71 (55 tilemap words changed in scene $D0), sets the flag word, clears actor flag $0008 and sets $0200 in the player's $10, writes player_character.LedgeJumpEntry into the player actor (address +$00, bank byte +$02, $08 and $2A zeroed) and dies. In Mesen2 the player's entry word became LedgeJumpEntry (animation $18, actor flags $8700) and the player fell; a narrow brick strip appeared in the dark pit south of the player.

Only the forced sequence was tested (the animation index was poked to $1C next to the actor): how the player reaches the gate in normal play, and what the two metatiles are meant to look like, was not watched. The jump starts because this script writes LedgeJumpEntry, with no type $08 cell involved (same as awB3_ledge_jump_trigger).
pyD4_falling_orb:
Falling orb of the Pyramid trickle area (scene $D4). The spawn byte picks the latch: flag = (spawn byte >> 1) + $80, so the first group (spawn byte #E5, tiles (22,1B), (24,1B), (22,1D), (24,1D)) uses $F2 and the second group (#E7, tiles (0C,4B), (0E,4B), (0C,4D), (0E,4D)) uses $F3. The four orbs of a group share the flag.

At load: with the flag set the orb is a fallen prop (priority minimum, collision cleared). With the flag clear it waits every frame for body bank $97 with animation index 1 on the player, characterForm 1 (Freedan) and the player within BranchIfPlayerNear #0C. On that trigger it sets the flag, waits 180 ticks (WaitByte #B3), waits a random delay, moves up by $100, plays the fall animation with sound $1515 and ends in the fallen state. The orbs do not fall on a timer and do not damage.

A sword hit (physical B, Will form works) runs the callback (code_08C456): with scratch flag $0F clear it sets $0F, marks the upper row pair y $2B-$2C solid and counts the slot word at $1060 + $26 down toward $FE00; at $FE00 it clears the lower row pair y $4B-$4C, plays the sound and clears $0F (about 26 frames when the word is already $FE00). While $0F is set (the upper barrier is still counting) the callback only jumps back to the idle state and the hit is ignored. The actor never tests characterForm or any other form state.
pyD6_vader_barrier_upper:
Upper Vader barrier of Pyramid scene $D6: the hit target that swaps the solid row pair y $2B-$2C (tiles $34-$39) for y $4B-$4C.

Idle state: solid rows y $2B-$2C are marked, y $4B-$4C are open, a hit callback (code_08C36C) is armed and the counter word at slot $1060 + $26 is $FE00. A sword hit (physical B, Will form works) runs the callback: with scratch flag $0F clear it sets $0F, marks the lower row pair y $4B-$4C solid and counts the slot word up from $FE00; when it reaches 0 (513 frames) it clears the upper row pair y $2B-$2C, plays the sound, clears $0F and re-arms the callback (the hit callback is not armed while the counter runs, so further swings in that window do not reach it). A callback entered with $0F already set (set by a lower barrier, or forced) only jumps back to the idle state and nothing changes; the lower barriers share the same flag. The actor never tests characterForm or any other form state.

sE6_gaia:
Dark Space / Gaia hub (scene $E6, the room reached from the Dark Space portals and from the diary menu's load) plus a shared character-transformation library (Bank 08, 579499-587528; GaiaNpcSprite and GaiaVoiceSparkle in Bank 09, 630928-630997). The same spawn list is also used by scene $09, which has no scene-meta entry. scene_meta_00E6 loads spm_darkspace_sprites ($0579 bytes) and plays track $16 (bgm_space_beyond_time).

=== STRUCTURE ===

DarkSpaceMainInit spawns three children with SpawnAfter: FireflySpawnerLoop, GaiaNpcSprite and GaiaVoiceSparkle. SpawnAfter inserts each new actor right after the parent, so the main actor's $06 link ends up on the LAST one spawned, the voice sparkle. Every 'LDY $06 / STA $0024, Y' below is therefore the voice sparkle's on / off switch ($FFFF = on, 0 = off), not an NPC interaction lock.
It then validates globalScriptIndex ($0AAC: the room variant, written by the portal actor or restored by the diary load; 4 or more becomes 0), keeps it in $0AB2 (saved with the game, restored by the diary menu), clears $0AAC and switch-cases to a layout: 0 DS_LayoutBasic (Gaia only), 1 DS_LayoutTransform (statues chosen by characterForm), 2 DS_LayoutAbility (ability orb chosen by the scene), 3 DS_LayoutSpecial (sets $0AAC = 1 and runs layout 1; this is the pyramid's Dark Space, where GaiaHint_AuraItem tests $0AAC and gives the Aura item).
Every room polls BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles zones (x1, y1, x2, y2 in tiles): Gaia (7,8)-(9,9) = GaiaDialogueEntry, left statue (3,A)-(5,B), right statue (B,A)-(D,B), exit (5,D)-(B,F) = DarkSpaceExit. Each room has a wait state (the player is still standing in a zone: nothing happens, so a dialogue cannot retrigger) and an active state that dispatches the zones; the *Wait / *TileWait pairs and the loc_ labels after them are these two states.
The called scripts (GaiaDialogueEntry, the *TransformDialogue routines) are entered with CallNear and end with RestoreSavedPtr, which returns to the room loop.

=== EXIT ===

DarkSpaceExit masks the joypad, hides the player ($10 |= $2000), puts this actor on him, plays SFX $0C on both channels and the dissolve animation $1C of spriteset_pickups_effects once, waits 30 ticks (WaitByte #1D), then fills the warp words: sceneNext = $0B12 (the scene the player warped from, saved by ExecuteWarp), player spawn X = $0B08 x 16 and Y = ($0B0C + 2) x 16 (the source warp rectangle's tile position), facing 3 and the packed camera window $0B10 / $0B11 -> warpScrollParams. gfxCacheIdxB = $0101 is the transition speed (exit and enter 1), gfxCacheIdxA = $0002 is exit effect 2 = mosaic, enter effect 0 = fade.

=== GAIA DIALOGUE ===

GaiaDialogueEntry: 6-tick pause (WaitByte #05), voice sparkle on, first visit (event flag $DC) the intro text, then GaiaHealAndHints. If HP < max it prints the 'hurt' text and writes hpToHeal = 40; UpdateHUD turns that request into +1 HP every 8 frames (SFX $0D) until HP = max (the loop yields until then). The hint is chosen by the position of the source scene in GaiaHintSceneTable (34 scenes, one GaiaHint_xx handler each; 21 of them have no text and go straight to the save prompt). GaiaSavePrompt: 'Record what's happened so far?' (DialogueOptions: entry 0 = cancel, 1 = first option, 2 = second option). Record = SaveGameState_Scene for the active slot ($0D8C), SFX $29, 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B), then 'Continue your journey?': Yes (entry 1) = GaiaThenGo, 'Then go.', returns to the room; No (entry 2) = GaiaThenRest, 'Then rest a while.', fades to track $0E (bgm_longing_for_the_past) and the actor yields forever. GaiaThenGo and GaiaThenRest are named after the answers 'Then go.' and 'Then rest a while.'; each is reached from two prompts.

=== FORMS AND ABILITIES ===

characterForm ($0AD4): 0 Will, 1 Freedan, 2 Shadow. A statue dialogue writes a Transform_* routine into the player actor's entry pointer ($0000 / $0002, $0008 = 0) and sets playerFlags $0800; the player then plays it (player body entry #05, the transformation frames), the routine sets characterForm and DarkSpaceRestoreControl clears $0800 and sends the player back to PlayerIdleEntry. The Shadow statue needs event flag $B4, whose only writer is daC8_neil (the Neil reunion in the Dao dormitory); first Freedan visit flag $F7, first Shadow visit flag $DD.
The Transform_* routines are a shared library: Transform_WillToShadow is entered from sE5_epilogue, pyDD_mummy_queen, gw8A_sand_fanger, mu67_vampires, sg55_viper, ir29_castoth and btE4_kara; Transform_ShadowToWill from pyDD_mummy_queen, gw8A_sand_fanger, mu67_vampires, sg55_viper, ir29_castoth and pyCD_jackal; Transform_FreedanToWill from sg55_mystic_statue, ir29_transform, ir1C_lily, ec13_lily, pyCD_jackal and mu67_bomb (13 files in all).
AbilitySceneTable has 6 entries of (scene, abilityBitmask bit): $15 Psycho Dash $01, $62 Psycho Slider $02, $86 Spin Dash $04, $42 Dark Friar $10, $A7 Aura Barrier $20, $B8 Earthquaker $40, ended by $00. The low nibble holds the Will abilities, the high nibble the Freedan abilities. The table position is the ability index used by AbilityNameTable (names) and AbilityDescriptionTable (descriptions) through globalScriptIndex. DS_LayoutAbility shows the orb for the current scene (BG change $86 and orb at (64,109) for a Will ability, $8B and (64,84) for a Freedan ability); AbilityOrbActor dies when the bit is already in abilityBitmask, otherwise waits for the player at the statue zone, turns him into the form that can use it (Will for the low nibble, Freedan for the high nibble) with LookupAbilityForm, ORs the bit in, plays the orb flight, fanfare (track $18) and the two texts.

=== SPRITES (spm_darkspace_sprites) ===

Animation #00 (4 frames, hold $63 then $0C x 3) is GaiaNpcSprite; #01 to #03 are the three sparkle variants of GaiaVoiceSparkle; #0A (32 frames of hold 0, a 16 x 16 spark alternating with an 8 x 8 tile) is the ability orb. #04 to #09 are not selected by this file (#04 to #06 are 8 x 8 effect tiles, #07 to #09 a 32 x 32 figure of 16 x 16 parts); the spm_darkspace_sprites block note lists all eleven animations. FireflyParticle and DarkSpaceExit use spriteset_pickups_effects.

=== NOT REFERENCED ===

No reference was found in extracted/ for: DS_AuraItemRoom and its handlers, AuraItemInteraction and its helpers (with dialogstring_08EFEF / 08F003 / 08F060), DarkSpaceAmbientParticle, the code at loc_08DA6B / loc_08DA77 (after an unconditional BRA), and the unused hint strings dialogstring_08DEC6, 08E066, 08E0C7, 08E109, 08E19C, 08E261, 08E2B9 and 08E615.

For the Aura cluster (DS_AuraItemRoom, AuraItemInteraction, AuraItemGrant, AuraItemInventoryFull, AuraItemReturnToWait, dialogstring_08EFEF / 08F003 / 08F060) 'no reference' means no reference in extracted code. baserom/patches/APUWaitFixes.patch.asm rewrites AuraItemGrant (AuraItemGrant!) and uses AuraItemInventoryFull and dialogstring_08EFEF.

The loop writes CGADSUB = $21 every frame and, when Will is inside the relative tile rectangle (32,3E)-(34,3F), queues scene $E3 at ($0280,$01A0) and dies (the same destination as the Solid Arm defeat). sEA_solid_arm:
Solid Arm boss fight -- Jeweler Gem's true form (scene $EA, enemy row 04, enemy number $5F).

Spawn: sets cameraBoundsY, spawns the defeat watcher (code_08F9F2), stores the revive warp (binary_08F9EA), locks the joypad ($EFFC), waits, plays sound #0E and applies BG change #9C. With flag $E8 clear it fades in music #1B, waits 289 ticks (WaitWord #$0120), SETS $E8 and prints the introduction ('Welcome to my home. The Jeweler Gem is a temporary form. The true form is called Solid Arm. ... It is I who manipulated the labor trade.'); with $E8 set (a repeat visit) the music fade, the dialog and the flag write are skipped. Because $E8 is set before the fight, the Jeweler Gem NPC (actors/jeweler_gem) disappears as soon as the introduction starts, even if Will dies. Then music #0F, a 50-tick wait (WaitByte #31), unlock, and the fight loop (arm attacks chosen by the player's Y and X position).

Defeat (code_08F9F2, polling enemiesRemaining): locks the joypad, fades in music #1B, waits 289 ticks (WaitWord #$0120), prints 'I was defeated again... Blazer was strong, but you are stronger... Danger approaches this planet. You should hurry to the Tower of Babel...' and queues scene $E3 at ($0280,$01A0). No item, flag or counter changes on defeat; nothing in the code rewards the Red Jewel collection.
